scenario.name: Black Basta Teams Vishing, Quick Assist, Backstab EDR Bypass & ChaCha20 (AA24-131A)
scenario.overview: Imagine a sunlit city park with green lawns, shade trees, winding stone footpaths, wooden benches, and a tiered stone water fountain at the center. Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the central park stone fountain. A watchful park ranger at the corner kiosk notices the exact same bench receiving repeated timed drop-offs and logs the suspicious pattern on the patrol board. In this scenario (T1566.004, Black Basta Teams Vishing, Quick Assist, Backstab EDR Bypass & ChaCha20 (AA24-131A)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: email Bombing, External Microsoft Teams, then backstab EDR Handle Killer, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Email Bombing, External Microsoft Teams, then Backstab EDR Handle Killer, then vssadmin Shadow Wipe, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Email Bombing, External Microsoft Teams Vishing & QuickAssist.exe Abuse
stages.subtitle: Initial Access (T1566.004 - Spearphishing Voice / T1219 - Remote Access Software)
stages.description: Strolling along the city park footpath like an ordinary afternoon walker, a covert courier sits on a wooden bench near the stone fountain and tapes a coded note underneath the armrest. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the park gate footpath in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the park ranger go about their routine. Storm-1811 bombarded the target’s corporate email address with thousands of automated newsletter registrations (creating both distraction and a believable pretext for an urgent IT call, while burying real security alert emails in the flood), then initiated an external federated Microsoft Teams call impersonating "IT Help Desk" and instructed the user to launch C:\Windows\System32\QuickAssist.exe (a pre-installed, Microsoft-signed remote support binary that establishes an encrypted outbound screen-sharing and remote-control session via *.remoteassistance.support.services.microsoft.com). Because QuickAssist.exe is natively included in Windows 10/11 and communicates exclusively with legitimate *.microsoft.com relay servers over HTTPS, standard perimeter firewalls and web proxies allow the session by default. In the documented EventID 1 exchange from Storm-1811 / Black Basta Operator to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK 1 (confirming that the C:WindowsSystem32QuickAssist.exe request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: Backstab EDR Handle Killer & SoftPerfect / Rclone Lateral Staging). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ C:\Windows\System32\QuickAssist.exe / ⇠#1 ACK 1) from Node ① (#1 Storm-1811 / Black Basta Operator) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Shares (.basta ChaCha20)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Backstab EDR Handle Killer & SoftPerfect / Rclone Lateral Staging
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Discovery (T1562.001 / T1046)
stages.description: Minutes later, an accomplice walks past the central park fountain, retrieves the hidden slip from the bench without speaking a word, and drops a replacement set of instructions. Here in Step 2 inside the city park, the intruder moves quietly past the park gate footpath into neighboring restricted rooms without disturbing the quiet botanical greenhouse. Inside the QuickAssist.exe session, the operator used curl.exe or msiexec.exe to stage payloads, executed Backstab (backstab.exe -n MsMpEng.exe -k, an open-source BYOVD utility that loads the signed Sysinternals PROCEXP.SYS driver to enumerate and forcibly close every kernel object and file handle held by Protected Process Light EDR agents), scanned internal subnets with SoftPerfect Network Scanner (netscan.exe), and exfiltrated sensitive shares using rclone.exe. Closing all kernel handles held by an EDR process via Backstab renders the security sensor deaf and unable to inspect files or processes even if the main user-mode .exe appears running in Task Manager. In the documented EventID 1 exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Microsoft Teams External Federation, Microsoft Teams External Federation responds with ALERT 1 (confirming that the C:UsersPublic ackstab.exe -n MsMpEng.exe -k request succeeded on Microsoft Teams External Federation and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: vssadmin Shadow Wipe & Black Basta ChaCha20/RSA-4096 Encryption (.basta)). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ C:\Users\Public\backstab.exe -n MsMpEng.exe -k / ⇠#2 ALERT 1) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Microsoft Teams External Federation), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Shares (.basta ChaCha20)).

keySpecs.value: backstab.exe -p MsMpEng.exe -k -d C:\Users\Public\PROCEXP.SYS (Closes all kernel handles held by EDR)
Monitor child processes spawned during active `QuickAssist.exe` sessions (`cmd.exe`, `powershell.exe`, `msiexec.exe`, `curl.exe`) and block `PROCEXP.SYS` via WDAC.

stages.title: Stage 3: vssadmin Shadow Wipe & Black Basta ChaCha20/RSA-4096 Encryption (.basta)
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact / T1490)
stages.description: Hidden in plain sight among joggers and park visitors, the pair moves confidential slips across the open park lawn without ever stepping near the guarded city hall across the street. In this final step inside the city park, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the central park stone fountain until the park kiosk patrol log catches the mismatch. Pivoting across the domain with PsExec or WMI, the operator ran vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet to destroy Volume Shadow Copies and executed the C++ Black Basta encryptor (basta.exe -forcepath, which uses a multi-threaded XChaCha20 stream cipher to encrypt 64-byte blocks alternating with 128-byte unencrypted gaps for maximum throughput, protects the per-file key with RSA-4096, appends .basta, and drops readme.faa.txt). By encrypting 64 bytes and skipping 128 bytes across large files, Black Basta corrupts multi-terabyte file servers in minutes before administrators can pull network cables. In the documented EventID 11 exchange from Microsoft Teams External Federation to Workstation (QuickAssist.exe Session), Workstation (QuickAssist.exe Session) responds with ACK 11 (confirming that the basta.exe request succeeded on Workstation (QuickAssist.exe Session) and completing the final execution objective of Black Basta Teams Vishing, Quick Assist, Backstab EDR Bypass & ChaCha20 (AA24-131A)). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ basta.exe / ⇠#3 ACK 11) from Node ③ (#3 Microsoft Teams External Federation) to Node ④ (#4 Workstation (QuickAssist.exe Session)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Enterprise Shares (.basta ChaCha20)).
